notice: Every number below is a PLACEHOLDER assumption, not a market fact. Section 5.3 of the concept proposal requires trial batches to measure input weight, output weight, yield, time, spoilage and unit cost before profitability is claimed. Replace these values with measured trials (ProductTrial) and the engine will prefer the measurements over the assumptions.

products.name: Matooke flour
products.tagline: Peeled, chipped, dried and milled - long shelf life, widest buyer set
products.demand_basis: Assumption: steady interest from bakeries, schools and urban households; must be confirmed with buyer interviews.
process_steps: Sort and wash; reject damaged or over-ripe fingers
Peel (manual or mechanical)
Slice into 4-8 mm chips
Optional blanch to reduce browning
Dry to below 10 % moisture: solar dome or mechanical dryer, turned regularly
Mill, sieve, pack in moisture-barrier bags with label
products.quality_spec: Off-white to cream flour, no dark specks, moisture <= 10 %, no rancid or fermented smell, 500 g / 1 kg / 5 kg sealed packs
food_safety: Processed product needs a UNBS quality mark / Usafe-type certificate for pre-packaged sale
Registration with the food authority is required for a processing premises
Labelling must show product name, net weight, ingredients,batch lot, packing date and best-before
products.capital_note: Dryer plus mill is the main capital item; a partner mill can be used at first instead of buying one.
risks: Sun drying on open ground risks dust, insects and aflatoxin-type mould if drying is slow
Moisture above 10 % leads to caking and spoilage in the pack
products.sourcing_note: Margin depends on buying fresh material cheaply - typically farmgate in a glut month. At Kampala market prices for a bunch, flour milling does not pay; the 'when to sell' module and this module have to be read together.

products.name: Dried matooke chips (unsweetened)
products.tagline: Simplest route: slice, dry, pack - can be cooked by the end buyer
products.demand_basis: Assumption: sold in local markets and to households that already know the product; needs a demand check before scaling.
process_steps: Peel and slice thick (8-12 mm)
Soak briefly in clean water to remove latex
Solar dry on raised mesh trays, turned twice a day
Sort by size and colour, pack in sealed bags
equipment: solar dome or shaded airy shed
products.quality_spec: Even cream colour, no mould, no insect damage, snaps rather than bends when properly dry
food_safety: Drying surfaces must be food-grade and off the ground
Batch record with input weight, output weight, date and operator
products.capital_note: Lowest capital of the listed options - a good first trial product for a farmer group.

products.name: Fried matooke crisps (salted, packaged)
products.tagline: Highest price per kg, but needs frying control and a real brand
products.demand_basis: Assumption: snack aisle and event catering demand exists but is competitive with potato crisps; test small packs first.
process_steps: Select firm mature fingers, peel, slice 1.5-2 mm
Blanch or soak, drain and dry surface moisture
Fry in clean palm/vegetable oil at 150-165 C
Drain, salt/season, cool fully before packing
Pack in metallised moisture-barrier bags with nitrogen if affordable
products.quality_spec: Uniform golden colour, low grease feel, crisp texture, no rancid smell, intact pieces >= 85 % by weight
food_safety: Oil must be monitored for reuse limits (polar compounds / smoke point) - a real food-safety issue
Rancidity is the main shelf-life risk; light and oxygen must be excluded
products.capital_note: Moderate equipment, high packaging and branding cost per kg sold.
risks: Returns from stale or broken product

products.name: Matooke-porridge blend flour (family / child feeding)
products.tagline: Flour blended with soya and amaranth - value from the blend, not the matooke
products.additives: Roasted soya flour and amaranth/flaxseed at agreed ratios (fixed recipe, batch-recorded)
products.demand_basis: Assumption: NGOs, health-worker channels and urban mothers; any nutrition claim requires approval - do not print one.
process_steps: Produce matooke flour as above
Roast and mill soya separately
Blend to a fixed recipe with a calibrated scale
Sieve, pack, label with full ingredient list and allergen statement
products.quality_spec: Consistent composition between batches, no lumps, declared soya allergen on label
food_safety: Any fortified/infant-positioning product draws extra scrutiny: get the recipe, labelling and claims reviewed before sale
Do not state that it treats or prevents malnutrition
products.capital_note: Blend precision matters more than machinery here.
risks: Claims that are not approved create legal exposure

products.name: Peeled parboiled matooke (frozen)
products.tagline: Convenience for kitchens - but only where cold chain is reliable
products.demand_basis: Assumption: hotels and caterers value labour savings; power cuts and freezer cost kill margins without a reliable chain.
process_steps: Peel into acidulated water
Parboil to agreed time, cool fast in clean cold water
Drain, pack by weight, blast freeze, keep at -18 C
Deliver in insulated boxes with temperature log
products.quality_spec: Firm texture, no browning, core temperature <= -18 C on delivery, no thaw-refreeze
food_safety: Temperature abuse is the main hazard; a broken chain means the batch is not sold as frozen product
products.capital_note: Highest capital and running cost of the options; do not attempt before a signed buyer.
risks: Freezer and transport cost per kg
